name: com.nextupwalkin/nextup-walk-in
title: NextUp Walk-in
description: Find barbers, salons, groomers and more with live walk-in waits, then join the line or book a time.

tools.name: find_walk_in_places
tools.description: Find businesses that take walk-ins, by US city, near a point, by the business's name or by ZIP code, with how long the wait is right now. Open places come first, shortest wait first. Use it when someone wants to go now without an appointment: a walk-in visit near them, who has the shortest wait, who is taking walk-ins today, how long the line is, or to check in online before they go. It covers live walk-in lines, not reviews or ratings, and not restaurant tables. Optionally narrow to one kind of business with `trade`: barbershops (barbershop), hair-salons (hair salon), nail-salons (nail salon), brow-and-lash (brow and lash studio), massage-and-spas (massage studio or spa), tattoo-shops (tattoo shop), pet-groomers (pet groomer), vet-clinics (vet clinic), chiropractors (walk-in chiropractor), tax-preparers (tax preparation office), auto-repair (auto repair shop), car-washes (car wash), phone-repair (phone repair shop). Returns at most 10 places, each with its slug, city, wait and a link to join the line. Pass `name` (part of a business or location name, any case) to look up a specific place without knowing its city, e.g. "how long is the wait at Fade Factor on Gum Branch"; then city and state are optional and only narrow the match. For "near me" questions, pass `latitude` and `longitude` (the person's own, or the assistant's knowledge of a place they named) to find places within `radiusMiles` (1 to 50, default 10), or pass city and state with `radiusMiles` to search around that town (only a town with listed places has a known center; for any other town give its latitude and longitude); each place then has `miles`, and open places come first, then nearest. Pass `zip` (5 digits) to find places whose address is in that exact ZIP code only; it doesn't search nearby ZIPs, so for "near" use a radius search around the town instead. Give city and state, or latitude and longitude, or name, or zip. Each place has `openNow` (its line takes check-ins now), `hoursToday` and `outsidePostedHours`: true means the business opened its line early or kept it open late, which is its choice, so say the line is taking check-ins outside its posted hours rather than calling it a mistake. `waitMinutes` is null when the place doesn't work out minutes: give `peopleWaiting` as a count then, never turn it into minutes. `updatedAt` is when the waits were read (UTC). Pass `service` (a few words, e.g. "oil change", "gel manicure", "beard trim") with any of those to keep only places that publicly list a service with those words in its name; each place then has `service` (`id`, `name`, `price`, `minutes`) for its best match. `price` is exactly as the place shows it ("$30", "from $45", empty when the place hides it): compare it across places for "cheapest" questions, and say when a place doesn't show a price. `minutes` is only there when the place shows lengths. The service `id` works with available_times, join_link and booking_link. It checks the first 30 places in the usual order, so narrow by city, radius or trade for a wider search. Start here when you don't have a place's slug yet; use get_place for one place's full details. If nothing is listed in that city or radius (or for that trade), it says so and names up to 3 nearest cities that do have places (with `miles` when known) instead of returning places; if no place has a matching service, it says so.

city.description: City name, e.g. Austin. Required with state unless name or zip is given

state.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX. Required with city

name.description: Optional part of a business or location name to look up, e.g. Fade Factor

zip.description: Optional 5-digit US ZIP code, e.g. 80302; matches the ZIP on places' addresses

latitude.description: Optional latitude in degrees (-90 to 90) to search near; needs longitude; not with name or zip

longitude.description: Optional longitude in degrees (-180 to 180) to search near; needs latitude. US longitudes are negative (west), e.g. -97.74 for Austin

radiusMiles.description: Optional search radius in miles, 1 to 50 (default 10); with latitude and longitude, or with city and state

trade.description: Optional kind of business, one of the slugs listed in the tool description

service.description: Optional service to look for, a few words, e.g. oil change; works with every other option

tools.name: get_place
tools.description: Details for one place from its `slug` (from find_walk_in_places): its address, whether its line is taking check-ins now (`openNow`), today's posted hours and the next seven days' hours (`hoursThisWeek`, starting today, null when none are posted), the current wait and how many people are waiting, whether it takes walk-ins and online bookings, its team members (with the ids that available_times, join_link and booking_link accept), and the link to join the line. When `outsidePostedHours` is true the business opened its line early or kept it open late (its choice, not an error): tell the person the line is taking check-ins outside its posted hours, with the hours, rather than saying it is open as usual. When `openNow` is false nobody new can join, though `peopleWaiting` may still be above 0 while the team finishes the line. `waitMinutes` is an estimate only where the place works it out from services; null means give the count, not minutes. Use it after find_walk_in_places, before linking the person anywhere. An unknown slug returns a not-found message.

tools.name: get_services
tools.description: The services a place offers publicly, with the prices and lengths it shows to customers (up to 30), each with an id. Use a service's id with available_times, join_link or booking_link. If the place doesn't list services online, it says so: send the person join_link and they choose there.

tools.name: available_times
tools.description: Open start times (up to 12) on one date for one service, when the place takes online bookings. Times are in the place's own time zone. Pass `memberId` (from get_place) to see only that team member's times. Use it when the person wants an appointment and asks when; then give them booking_link. For walking in now, use join_link instead. If the place doesn't take online bookings, the service isn't offered, or the day is full, it says so (try another date).

date.description: Date as YYYY-MM-DD, in the place's time zone

memberId.description: Optional team member id from get_place

tools.name: join_link
tools.description: A link the person taps to join the place's line from their phone, optionally with a service and team member filled in. You cannot join for them: they confirm on the place's own page. Use it for walking in now; for a set time later, use booking_link. If the place isn't taking check-ins right now, or that service or team member isn't available there, it says so instead of returning a link.

memberId.description: Optional team member id from get_place

tools.name: booking_link
tools.description: A link the person taps to book an appointment, with the service (and optionally a team member and date) filled in. You cannot book for them: they pick a time and confirm on the place's own page. Use it for an appointment at a set time (check available_times first if they ask when); for walking in now, use join_link. If the place doesn't take online bookings, it says so: offer join_link instead.

memberId.description: Optional team member id from get_place

tools.name: best_time_to_visit
tools.description: When to come for the shortest wait at one place on a day, from that place's own past visits on that weekday over the last 8 weeks: the best time, the expected wait then, the expected wait through the day, and how busy each hour usually is. Pass `date` (YYYY-MM-DD in the place's time zone, today through 6 days ahead; default today). These are estimates, not promises: say "about". Use it when someone asks when it's least busy or when to come; for the wait right now use get_place. If the place is closed that day or hasn't enough past visits, it says so instead.

date.description: Optional date as YYYY-MM-DD, today through 6 days ahead (default today)

tools.name: check_my_place_in_line
tools.description: How the person's own visit is going, from the link in their check-in text (https://app.nextupwalkin.com/w/…) or on their status page (https://app.nextupwalkin.com/q/…?t=…): whether they are still waiting, how many people are ahead of them, about how many minutes (only where the place works minutes out; otherwise give the count), and whether and when they were called. Use it when the person who checked in asks how much longer, what number they are or whether they've been called, and gives or pastes that link. The link is private to that person: never ask for anyone else's, and don't repeat it or its `t` code back. It returns nothing personal (no names, phone numbers or notes) and changes nothing. Estimates, not a promise: say "about". If the link doesn't work it says so.

link.description: The status link from the person's check-in text or page, like https://app.nextupwalkin.com/q/…?t=…

tools.name: purchase_link
tools.description: The packages and memberships a place sells online, and the link where the person pays for them. Only for places whose owner turned it on. You cannot pay for them: they open the link and pay on the place's own secure Stripe page. Gift cards aren't sold through this tool: if the person asks, say they can buy one from the place's own page (join_link) when the place sells them.
